描述_EN: the pockets have been tailored to ensure there is no break in this design. sleeveless jackets like this were usually worn over long robes and the slits at the sides allowed for expansion. this waistcoat is made from closely woven black ribbed silk and it has a subdued pattern of lattice roundels woven into it. this waistcoat has shoulder seams and the back is cut from one piece of cloth, which, like the pockets, are a sign of twentieth-century tailoring. the garment is versatile enough to be worn with western clothes and this may well have been how it was used. it was part of the bequest left too the v&a by sir john addis and, as a diplomat in china, he seems to have had several chinese-style garments made especially for him. this was a time when chinese men started wearing western three-piece suits or a mix of chinese and western modes. the match across the sewing lines is meticulous as is that across the fold-line at the top of the pocket. chinese garments did not originally have pockets like these but, by the beginning of the twentieth century, they were being added to traditional styles.
描述_ZN: 口袋是量身定做的，以确保在这个设计中没有断裂。 像这样的无袖夹克通常穿在长袍外面，两侧的缝隙允许扩张。 这件马甲是由紧密编织的黑色罗纹丝制成的，它有一个低调的格子圆形图案编织而成。 这件马甲有肩缝，背部是由一块布裁剪而成的，这和口袋一样，是二十世纪裁缝的标志。 这件衣服的用途很广，可以和西方的衣服一起穿，这很可能就是它的用途。 这是John Addis先生留给V&A的遗产的一部分，作为一名驻中国的外交官，他似乎特别为他制作了几件中国风格的服装。 这是个中国男人开始穿西方三件套或中西方混合模式的时期。 整个缝制线的匹配是一丝不苟的，就像口袋顶部的折线一样。 中国服装最初没有这样的口袋，但到了20世纪初，传统的服装款式中开始有了口袋。
